1 Ejemplo 1: base transaccional pequeña

transacciones_lista <- list(
  c("pan", "leche", "huevos"),
  c("pan", "leche"),
  c("pan", "mantequilla"),
  c("leche", "huevos"),
  c("pan", "leche", "mantequilla"),
  c("pan", "huevos"),
  c("leche", "mantequilla"),
  c("pan", "leche", "huevos", "mantequilla")
)

transacciones <- as(transacciones_lista, "transactions")
transacciones
## transactions in sparse format with
##  8 transactions (rows) and
##  4 items (columns)
summary(transacciones)
## transactions as itemMatrix in sparse format with
##  8 rows (elements/itemsets/transactions) and
##  4 columns (items) and a density of 0.625 
## 
## most frequent items:
##       leche         pan      huevos mantequilla     (Other) 
##           6           6           4           4           0 
## 
## element (itemset/transaction) length distribution:
## sizes
## 2 3 4 
## 5 2 1 
## 
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##     2.0     2.0     2.0     2.5     3.0     4.0 
## 
## includes extended item information - examples:
##        labels
## 1      huevos
## 2       leche
## 3 mantequilla
inspect(transacciones)
##     items                            
## [1] {huevos, leche, pan}             
## [2] {leche, pan}                     
## [3] {mantequilla, pan}               
## [4] {huevos, leche}                  
## [5] {leche, mantequilla, pan}        
## [6] {huevos, pan}                    
## [7] {leche, mantequilla}             
## [8] {huevos, leche, mantequilla, pan}
matriz_items <- as(transacciones, "matrix")
matriz_items
##      huevos leche mantequilla   pan
## [1,]   TRUE  TRUE       FALSE  TRUE
## [2,]  FALSE  TRUE       FALSE  TRUE
## [3,]  FALSE FALSE        TRUE  TRUE
## [4,]   TRUE  TRUE       FALSE FALSE
## [5,]  FALSE  TRUE        TRUE  TRUE
## [6,]   TRUE FALSE       FALSE  TRUE
## [7,]  FALSE  TRUE        TRUE FALSE
## [8,]   TRUE  TRUE        TRUE  TRUE
itemFrequency(transacciones, type = "absolute")
##      huevos       leche mantequilla         pan 
##           4           6           4           6
itemFrequency(transacciones, type = "relative")
##      huevos       leche mantequilla         pan 
##        0.50        0.75        0.50        0.75
itemFrequencyPlot(
  transacciones,
  topN = 10,
  type = "absolute",
  main = "Frecuencia absoluta de ítems"
)

2 Ejemplo 2: cálculo manual de métricas

n <- length(transacciones)
X <- "pan"
Y <- "leche"

mat <- as(transacciones, "matrix")

soporte_X <- sum(mat[, X]) / n
soporte_Y <- sum(mat[, Y]) / n
soporte_XY <- sum(mat[, X] & mat[, Y]) / n

confianza_X_Y <- soporte_XY / soporte_X
lift_X_Y <- confianza_X_Y / soporte_Y
leverage_X_Y <- soporte_XY - soporte_X * soporte_Y
conviction_X_Y <- (1 - soporte_Y) / (1 - confianza_X_Y)

metricas <- tibble(
  regla = paste(X, "=>", Y),
  soporte_X = soporte_X,
  soporte_Y = soporte_Y,
  soporte_XY = soporte_XY,
  confianza = confianza_X_Y,
  lift = lift_X_Y,
  leverage = leverage_X_Y,
  conviction = conviction_X_Y
)

metricas
## # A tibble: 1 × 8
##   regla       soporte_X soporte_Y soporte_XY confianza  lift leverage conviction
##   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 pan => lec…      0.75      0.75        0.5     0.667 0.889  -0.0625       0.75
tabla_XY <- table(
  X_presente = mat[, X],
  Y_presente = mat[, Y]
)

tabla_XY
##           Y_presente
## X_presente FALSE TRUE
##      FALSE     0    2
##      TRUE      2    4
fisher.test(tabla_XY)
## 
##  Fisher's Exact Test for Count Data
## 
## data:  tabla_XY
## p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: true odds ratio is not equal to 1
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##   0.00000 18.92032
## sample estimates:
## odds ratio 
##          0
chisq.test(tabla_XY, correct = FALSE)
## 
##  Pearson's Chi-squared test
## 
## data:  tabla_XY
## X-squared = 0.88889, df = 1, p-value = 0.3458

3 Ejemplo 3: reglas con Apriori

reglas <- apriori(
  transacciones,
  parameter = list(
    supp = 0.25,
    conf = 0.60,
    minlen = 2
  )
)
## Apriori
## 
## Parameter specification:
##  confidence minval smax arem  aval originalSupport maxtime support minlen
##         0.6    0.1    1 none FALSE            TRUE       5    0.25      2
##  maxlen target  ext
##      10  rules TRUE
## 
## Algorithmic control:
##  filter tree heap memopt load sort verbose
##     0.1 TRUE TRUE  FALSE TRUE    2    TRUE
## 
## Absolute minimum support count: 2 
## 
## set item appearances ...[0 item(s)] done [0.00s].
## set transactions ...[4 item(s), 8 transaction(s)] done [0.00s].
## sorting and recoding items ... [4 item(s)] done [0.00s].
## creating transaction tree ... done [0.00s].
## checking subsets of size 1 2 3 done [0.00s].
## writing ... [10 rule(s)] done [0.00s].
## creating S4 object  ... done [0.00s].
reglas
## set of 10 rules
summary(reglas)
## set of 10 rules
## 
## rule length distribution (lhs + rhs):sizes
## 2 3 
## 6 4 
## 
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##     2.0     2.0     2.0     2.4     3.0     3.0 
## 
## summary of quality measures:
##     support        confidence        coverage          lift       
##  Min.   :0.250   Min.   :0.6667   Min.   :0.375   Min.   :0.8889  
##  1st Qu.:0.250   1st Qu.:0.6667   1st Qu.:0.375   1st Qu.:0.8889  
##  Median :0.375   Median :0.6667   Median :0.500   Median :0.8889  
##  Mean   :0.350   Mean   :0.7000   Mean   :0.500   Mean   :0.9333  
##  3rd Qu.:0.375   3rd Qu.:0.7500   3rd Qu.:0.500   3rd Qu.:1.0000  
##  Max.   :0.500   Max.   :0.7500   Max.   :0.750   Max.   :1.0000  
##      count    
##  Min.   :2.0  
##  1st Qu.:2.0  
##  Median :3.0  
##  Mean   :2.8  
##  3rd Qu.:3.0  
##  Max.   :4.0  
## 
## mining info:
##           data ntransactions support confidence

4 Ejemplo 4: filtrado de reglas

reglas_leche <- subset(reglas, rhs %in% "leche")
inspect(sort(reglas_leche, by = "confidence", decreasing = TRUE))
##     lhs                   rhs     support confidence coverage lift      count
## [1] {huevos}           => {leche} 0.375   0.7500000  0.500    1.0000000 3    
## [2] {mantequilla}      => {leche} 0.375   0.7500000  0.500    1.0000000 3    
## [3] {pan}              => {leche} 0.500   0.6666667  0.750    0.8888889 4    
## [4] {huevos, pan}      => {leche} 0.250   0.6666667  0.375    0.8888889 2    
## [5] {mantequilla, pan} => {leche} 0.250   0.6666667  0.375    0.8888889 2
reglas_pan_lhs <- subset(reglas, lhs %in% "pan")
inspect(sort(reglas_pan_lhs, by = "lift", decreasing = TRUE))
##     lhs                   rhs     support confidence coverage lift      count
## [1] {pan}              => {leche} 0.50    0.6666667  0.750    0.8888889 4    
## [2] {huevos, pan}      => {leche} 0.25    0.6666667  0.375    0.8888889 2    
## [3] {mantequilla, pan} => {leche} 0.25    0.6666667  0.375    0.8888889 2
reglas_fuertes <- subset(reglas, confidence >= 0.7 & lift > 1)
inspect(sort(reglas_fuertes, by = "lift", decreasing = TRUE))

5 Ejemplo 5: reglas redundantes

reglas_ordenadas <- sort(reglas, by = "lift", decreasing = TRUE)
redundantes <- is.redundant(reglas_ordenadas)

reglas_no_redundantes <- reglas_ordenadas[!redundantes]

length(reglas_ordenadas)
## [1] 10
length(reglas_no_redundantes)
## [1] 6
inspect(reglas_no_redundantes)

6 Ejemplo 6: itemsets frecuentes con Apriori

itemsets_apriori <- apriori(
  transacciones,
  parameter = list(
    target = "frequent itemsets",
    supp = 0.25,
    minlen = 1
  )
)
## Apriori
## 
## Parameter specification:
##  confidence minval smax arem  aval originalSupport maxtime support minlen
##          NA    0.1    1 none FALSE            TRUE       5    0.25      1
##  maxlen            target  ext
##      10 frequent itemsets TRUE
## 
## Algorithmic control:
##  filter tree heap memopt load sort verbose
##     0.1 TRUE TRUE  FALSE TRUE    2    TRUE
## 
## Absolute minimum support count: 2 
## 
## set item appearances ...[0 item(s)] done [0.00s].
## set transactions ...[4 item(s), 8 transaction(s)] done [0.00s].
## sorting and recoding items ... [4 item(s)] done [0.00s].
## creating transaction tree ... done [0.00s].
## checking subsets of size 1 2 3 done [0.00s].
## sorting transactions ... done [0.00s].
## writing ... [11 set(s)] done [0.00s].
## creating S4 object  ... done [0.00s].
itemsets_apriori <- sort(itemsets_apriori, by = "support", decreasing = TRUE)
inspect(itemsets_apriori)
##      items                     support count
## [1]  {leche}                   0.750   6    
## [2]  {pan}                     0.750   6    
## [3]  {huevos}                  0.500   4    
## [4]  {mantequilla}             0.500   4

## [6]  {huevos, leche}           0.375   3    
## [7]  {huevos, pan}             0.375   3    
## [8]  {leche, mantequilla}      0.375   3    
## [9]  {mantequilla, pan}        0.375   3    
## [10] {huevos, leche, pan}      0.250   2    
## [11] {leche, mantequilla, pan} 0.250   2

7 Ejemplo 7: itemsets frecuentes con Eclat

itemsets_eclat <- eclat(
  transacciones,
  parameter = list(
    supp = 0.25,
    minlen = 1
  )
)
## Eclat
## 
## parameter specification:
##  tidLists support minlen maxlen            target  ext
##     FALSE    0.25      1     10 frequent itemsets TRUE
## 
## algorithmic control:
##  sparse sort verbose
##       7   -2    TRUE
## 
## Absolute minimum support count: 2 
## 
## create itemset ... 
## set transactions ...[4 item(s), 8 transaction(s)] done [0.00s].
## sorting and recoding items ... [4 item(s)] done [0.00s].
## creating bit matrix ... [4 row(s), 8 column(s)] done [0.00s].
## writing  ... [11 set(s)] done [0.00s].
## Creating S4 object  ... done [0.00s].
itemsets_eclat <- sort(itemsets_eclat, by = "support", decreasing = TRUE)
inspect(itemsets_eclat)
##      items                     support count
## [1]  {leche}                   0.750   6    
## [2]  {pan}                     0.750   6    
## [3]  {leche, pan}              0.500   4    
## [4]  {huevos}                  0.500   4    
## [5]  {mantequilla}             0.500   4    
## [6]  {leche, mantequilla}      0.375   3    
## [7]  {mantequilla, pan}        0.375   3    
## [8]  {huevos, leche}           0.375   3    
## [9]  {huevos, pan}             0.375   3    
## [10] {leche, mantequilla, pan} 0.250   2    
## [11] {huevos, leche, pan}      0.250   2

11 Ejemplo 13: grid de parámetros

parametros <- expand.grid(
  supp = c(0.001, 0.005, 0.01),
  conf = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6)
)

resultados_grid <- parametros %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    n_reglas = length(
      apriori(
        Groceries,
        parameter = list(
          supp = supp,
          conf = conf,
          minlen = 2,
          maxlen = 5
        ),
        control = list(verbose = FALSE)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

resultados_grid
## # A tibble: 9 × 3
##    supp  conf n_reglas
##   <dbl> <dbl>    <int>
## 1 0.001   0.2    21573
## 2 0.005   0.2      872
## 3 0.01    0.2      231
## 4 0.001   0.4     8901
## 5 0.005   0.4      270
## 6 0.01    0.4       62
## 7 0.001   0.6     2884
## 8 0.005   0.6       22
## 9 0.01    0.6        0
ggplot(resultados_grid, aes(x = supp, y = n_reglas, group = factor(conf))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ conf, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(
    x = "Soporte mínimo",
    y = "Número de reglas",
    title = "Número de reglas según soporte y confianza"
  )
